claim: OTLP is the standard card 6.1 Telemetry is checked against: it fixes how telemetry travels from a source through collectors to a backend, which is what makes the backend swappable.
query: OpenTelemetry protocol specification encoding transport delivery telemetry
snippet: The OpenTelemetry Protocol (OTLP) specification describes the encoding, transport, and delivery mechanism of telemetry data between telemetry sources, intermediate nodes such as collectors and telemetry backends.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: What the telemetry wire contract is

claim: The card's verb set is one operation, Export, in a request/response shape - the narrowest operation set of any card profiled so far.
snippet: OTLP is a request/response style protocol: the clients send requests, and the server replies with corresponding responses. This document defines one request and response type: Export.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: The operation set at this boundary

claim: A caller distinguishes full from partial acceptance by whether partial_success is set, not by the status code alone.
query: OTLP full success partial success response partial_success field
snippet: The server MUST leave the partial_success field unset in case of a successful response.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: Response outcome domain: success leaves partial_success unset

claim: Partial success is a third outcome beside success and failure, and it carries an explicit prohibition on retry.
query: OTLP client must not retry partial success response
snippet: The client MUST NOT retry the request when it receives a partial success response where the partial_success is populated.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: Response outcome domain: partial success is not retryable

claim: The specification types its failures into exactly two categories that decide the caller's retry behaviour.
snippet: When the server returns an error, it falls into 2 broad categories: retryable and non-retryable:
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry

claim: A non-retryable error obliges the client to drop the data rather than hold or resend it - a data-loss decision the standard makes explicitly.
query: OTLP non-retryable error client must not retry must drop telemetry
snippet: Non-retryable errors indicate that telemetry data processing failed, and the client MUST NOT retry sending the same telemetry data. The client MUST drop the telemetry data.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: Typed failures: what a non-retryable error obliges the client to do

claim: Compression is a caller-configurable word with a closed value set that applies at the transport step, not at the span.
query: OTLP transport compression options none gzip server components must support
snippet: All server components MUST support the following transport compression options: No compression, denoted by none. Gzip compression, denoted by gzip.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: The configurable words and the step they apply at

claim: One operation set, two transports - the same shape as card 1.5, where the binding rather than the library was the axis a second implementation had to differ on.
query: OTLP implemented over gRPC and HTTP transports protocol buffers schema
snippet: This specification defines how OTLP is implemented over gRPC and HTTP transports and specifies Protocol Buffers schema that is used for the payloads.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: The transports one operation set is carried over

snippet: Langfuse can operate as an OpenTelemetry Backend to receive traces on the /api/public/otel (OTLP) endpoint. In addition to the Langfuse SDKs and native integrations, this OpenTelemetry endpoint is designed to increase compatibility with frameworks, libraries, and languages beyond the SDKs and native integrations.
title: OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability - Langfuse

claim: Four signal-specific request messages are four payload shapes of the single Export operation, not four operations.
query: OTLP Export ServiceRequest messages logs metrics traces profiles unary
snippet: the client starts sending telemetry data using unary requests using Export*ServiceRequest messages (ExportLogsServiceRequest for logs, ExportMetricsServiceRequest for metrics, ExportTraceServiceRequest for traces, ExportProfilesServiceRequest for profiles).

claim: The single status code the specification names outright, and it is classified non-retryable rather than left to the caller to guess.
query: OTLP RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED non-retryable message size limit exceeded
snippet: If the limit is exceeded, the gRPC server implementations MUST report a RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED code as a non-retryable error.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry

claim: The backend is selected by an exporter environment variable, which means it is chosen before any span exists rather than per call.
title: OpenTelemetry (OTEL) for LLM Observability - Langfuse

claim: OTLP guarantees delivery for exactly one client/server hop and puts multi-hop end-to-end delivery out of scope, which is what makes collector-in-path versus direct-export a difference a caller can read rather than a label.
query: OTLP reliability one pair client server intermediary nodes collector end-to-end out of scope
snippet: Note: this protocol is concerned with the reliability of delivery between one pair of client/server nodes and aims to ensure that no data is lost in transit between the client and the server. Many telemetry collection systems have intermediary nodes that the data must travel across until reaching the final destination (e.g. application -> agent -> collector -> backend). End-to-end delivery guarantees in such systems is outside of the scope of OTLP.
title: OTLP Specification 1.11.0 | OpenTelemetry
topic: What the delivery guarantee does and does not span
